newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales off 1.0 pct in Nov - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales off 1.0 pct in Nov - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales fell 1.0 percent in the first three weeks of fiscal November versus October, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbok retail sales index.

The index rose 4.8 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 3.7 percent in the week ended November 23, compared with the same week a year ago, said the report.
A mismatch in weekly comparisons to Thanksgiving weeks are expected to result in a relatively weak November, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook research.
"Don't be mislead by the figures," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
The comparisons against the Thanksgiving week a year ago are skewing some figures, he said, adding that most retailers expected a decline.
However, Eilenberg noted that many retailers said they consider November results so far "to be as good as, or better than planned."
Apparel and accessories continued to lead in department and chain store sales, while discounters reported a pick-up in hard lines, Eilenberg said.
Sales are likely to get a boost immediately after Thanksgiving, but they won't be as significant as they used to be, Eilenberg said.
He said the weekend after Thanksgiving used to be the biggest shopping days of the year. "But that is no longer true ... The Saturday before Christmas is really the biggest shopping day of the year.
